predecessors.name: Kingdom of Macedon
predecessors.text: Egypt, which Alexander the Great 'conquered' in 332 BC; Ptolemy 'ruled Egypt from 323 BC, nominally in the name of the joint kings Philip III and Alexander IV'

successors.name: Roman Republic
successors.text: Egypt: 'The city passed, with the rest of Egypt, into Roman hands in 30 BC'

rulers.name: Ptolemy I Soter
rulers.title: satrap of Egypt from 323, king from 305

ledger.x: 323: Ptolemy takes Egypt as satrap.
323: Ptolemy holds Egypt as satrap of the joint kings.
322: Ptolemy's general Ophellas takes Cyrenaica.
321: Ptolemy's Egypt leaves the empire's tint.
318: Ptolemy occupies Syria and takes Laomedon.
318: Ptolemy places the Cypriot kings under his protection.
315: Ptolemy gives up Syria.
313: revolt in Cyrene.
313: the Cyrene revolt is crushed.
313: the protectorate over the Cypriot kings gives way to direct rule.
313: Ptolemy reconquers Cyprus.
312: Ptolemy fights for Syria.

311: peace. 'In 311, a peace was concluded between the combatants.' The Wars of the Diadochi page then has Ptolemy in control of 'Egypt, Syria, Cyrene and Cyprus'; the Ptolemy I page and Cliopatria show no Syria for Ptolemy until 302-301. [Repair pass: counterpart changed from antigonid-dynasty (which begins in 306)…
308: Ptolemy takes Corinth.
306: Demetrius takes Cyprus.
305: Ptolemy takes the title of king.
305: Cyrene rebels against Ptolemy.
305: the revolt of Cyrene against Ptolemy opens and is fought over until about 300 (cyrenaica /ledger/5).
304: Demetrius takes the Ptolemaic holdings on the isthmus.
302: Ptolemy invades Syria a third time.
301: Ptolemy holds Coele-Syria after Ipsus.
301: the fighting for Coele-Syria ends at Ipsus.
300: the revolt ends.
300: Magas reconquers Cyrene for Ptolemy.
295: Ptolemy retakes Cyprus.
274: Ptolemy II annexes Lower Nubia.
274: Cyrenaica breaks away under Magas.
274: the First Syrian War begins ('First Syrian War (274-271 BC)').
271: the First Syrian War ends in a Ptolemaic victory.
271: Ptolemy II wins the Anatolian coast.
260: the Second Syrian War begins ('Second Syrian War (260-253 BC)'); 'Antigonus' fleet defeated Ptolemy's at the Battle of Cos in 261 BC'.
253: the Second Syrian War ends, 'concluded around 253 BC with the marriage of Antiochus to Ptolemy's daughter'.
253: Ptolemy loses ground in Anatolia.
246: Cyrenaica returns to Egypt with Berenice II's marriage.
246: the Third Syrian War begins: 'Ptolemy declared war on Laodice's newly crowned son, Seleucus II, in 246 BC'; Ptolemy III 'briefly occupied Antioch' and reached Babylon.
246: the Cyclades pass to Antigonus Gonatas.
241: peace ends the Third Syrian War.
241: Ptolemy III at his height.
219: the Fourth Syrian War begins ('Fourth Syrian War (219-217 BC)'); Antiochus 'recaptured Seleucia Pieria as well as cities in Phoenicia, amongst them Tyre'.
219: Antiochus III retakes Seleucia Pieria, the port of Antioch, and Phoenician cities including Tyre.

217: Raphia. 'In the summer of 217 BC, Ptolemy engaged and defeated the long-delayed Antiochus'; 'Ptolemy's victory preserved his control over Coele-Syria, and the weak king declined to advance further'. Seleucia Pieria stayed Seleucid.
205: Upper Egypt secedes.
204: Kush takes Lower Nubia during the Theban revolt.
202: the Fifth Syrian War begins ('202/201-195 BC' in the page's table; the text dates no first campaign).
201: Philip V seizes Ptolemaic Samos, Miletus and Carian footholds.
199: Ptolemaic troops retake the Thebaid.
198: Coele-Syria is lost.
198: the Anatolian coast is lost.
198: the fighting for Coele-Syria ends; the treaty of 195 only confirms it.
197: the Thebaid is lost again.
195: the fighting at Asyut begins; 'heavy fighting from 195 to 191 BC' as Chaonnophris's territory expanded north toward Asyut.
191: the fighting at Asyut ends.
191: the army under Ptolemaios retakes Thebes ('retook control of Thebes the same year').
186: the revolt of the south is over.
186: the Ptolemies re-establish rule over Lower Nubia.
170: Antiochus IV invades Egypt.
168: the Seleucid forces leave.
163: Cyrene goes to Ptolemy VIII.
161: Ptolemy VIII invades Cyprus.
160: the Cyprus expedition is abandoned.
154: Ptolemy VI besieges his brother.
154: Ptolemy VIII gives up Cyprus.
145: Ptolemy VIII reunites the kingdom.
132: civil war in Egypt, 'from 132/1 to 127/6 BC, in which Cleopatra II controlled Alexandria'.
127: 'Cleopatra II took her treasury and fled Alexandria for the court of Demetrius II.
105: Cyrene becomes a separate kingdom.
58: Rome annexes Cyprus.
47: Caesar returns Cyprus to the Ptolemies.
36: Antony gives Cilicia Aspera to Cleopatra.
34: the Donations of Alexandria.
31: Cyprus returns to Rome after Actium.
30: Cleopatra's Cilicia Aspera passes to Rome.
30: Egypt passes to Rome.
30: the Ptolemaic Kingdom ends with the death of Cleopatra VII (12 August); Egypt, with Cyrenaica and central Syria, goes to Rome.

wars.name: Wars of the Diadochi
wars.outcome: Ptolemy keeps Egypt and Cyrenaica, loses Cyprus (306) and wins Coele-Syria at Ipsus (301).

wars.name: Magas' war against Ptolemy II
wars.outcome: Cyrenaica independent under Magas until his death in 250; Cyrenaica rejoined Egypt by the marriage of Berenice II to Ptolemy III.

wars.name: First Syrian War
wars.outcome: Ptolemaic victory: Ptolemy II reconquered the territories Antiochus I had taken, extending Ptolemaic rule into Caria and most of Cilicia.

wars.name: Second Syrian War
wars.outcome: Inconclusive: Ptolemy lost ground in Cilicia, Pamphylia and Ionia; Antiochus II regained Miletus and Ephesus; peace c.

wars.name: Third Syrian War
wars.outcome: Ptolemy III's conquests: victories in Syria and Anatolia, Antioch briefly occupied, Babylon reached; the 241 peace gave him the northern Syrian coast (Seleucia Pieria) at the zenith of Ptolemaic power.

wars.name: Fourth Syrian War
wars.outcome: Raphia (217): Ptolemy IV defeated Antiochus III and kept Coele-Syria; Seleucia Pieria stayed Seleucid.

wars.name: Great Theban Revolt
wars.outcome: The Thebaid broke away under Horwennefer/Haronnophris (205-199) and Ankhwennefer/Chaonnophris (c.

wars.name: Fifth Syrian War
wars.outcome: Antiochus III took Coele-Syria (subjugation complete 198) and raided the coastal strongholds in Caria and Cilicia; a treaty of 195 left him Coele-Syria and married Ptolemy V to Cleopatra I.

wars.name: Sixth Syrian War
wars.outcome: Antiochus IV took Pelusium, Memphis and Cyprus but failed to take Alexandria; after the Roman ultimatum at Eleusis he evacuated Egypt and Cyprus; revolts in Egypt 168-164.

wars.name: Ptolemy VI and Ptolemy VIII over Cyprus and Cyrene
wars.outcome: Ptolemy VIII, given Cyrene by Roman decision in 163, invaded Cyprus in 161 and was besieged and captured at Lapethus in 154; he left Cyprus to his brother and kept Cyrenaica.

wars.name: Ptolemaic civil war of 132-127
wars.outcome: Cleopatra II held Alexandria 132/1-127; she fled to the court of Demetrius II and Ptolemy VIII reconquered the city.

wars.name: War of Actium
wars.outcome: Octavian defeated Antony and Cleopatra; Cleopatra killed herself on 12 August 30 BC and Egypt passed to Rome.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey lines are given on the pages opened.
